summary.headline: Powerica Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.6% on commodity inflation; DC order book hit INR900 crore (INR1,100 crore by Aug 7).
summary.overview:
Revenue grew 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, with EBITDA of INR106 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR64 crore (8.3% margin). Management said elevated commodity and energy prices, a lag in passing costs to customers, and an adverse revenue mix compressed genset margins, with recovery expected from Q2-Q3 after two-phase price hikes. Order book as of July 31, 2026 was INR1,700 crore, of which data center orders were INR900 crore. Wind IPP portfolio visibility rose to about 638 MW after new awards, and FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated.</overview>

segments.name: DG sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: Order book of INR1,700 crore as of July 31, 2026, with data center orders at INR900 crore; genset EBITDA margin fell to 5.6% in Q1 on commodity costs and mix. Capacity utilisation 75-80% on one shift.

segments.name: Wind / IPP and EPC-BOP
segments.commentary: Wind is 18.6% of revenue, growing 28.8% YoY at a 48.6% EBITDA margin, helped by 51.3 MW added in Feb 2026. Owned IPP capacity is 330 MW, with a roadmap to about 638 MW.

segments.name: MSLG (defence/large projects)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on slower order booking because international inquiries were put on hold by the geopolitical situation. Won a INR41 crore tender to be executed in 12-15 months and has a large PSU order executable by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Allied business
segments.commentary: Contributed 9% of revenue; management attributed the slowdown to milestone-based project revenue recognition and defence product approval cycles of 1-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance reiterated.
Genset margins expected to stay subdued in Q1 and part of Q2 and improve from Q3 onward, per management; no formal margin guidance given for the DG business this year.
Order book up 15-19% YoY as of July 31, 2026, depending on product mix.
Data center order book expected to execute over 12-18 months; management expects data center at 20%+ of revenue on an annualised basis.
Wind pipeline: 50 MW to go live in Q4 FY27, 150 MW in FY28, and 100 MW the year after.
Management expects 250-300 MW of EPC/BOP execution per year, at about INR400 crore of top line.
capex_capacity: DG set capacity: one shift in operation, utilisation 75-80%; management says capacity is sufficient for current demand and can be expanded if needed.
IPP portfolio: 330 MW operating, targeting about 638 MW (management corrected 633.55 MW). 50 MW added this FY, 150 MW in FY28, 100 MW later.
New wind projects: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction; 50 MW GUVNL LOA awaited, with PPA expected Nov-Dec 2026; 100 MW SECI LOA received, PPA pending SECI call.
Two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Windfusion Renewable and Whisper Wind Renewable, set up for transmission connectivity; 49% stake acquired in Fuji-Kailash Energy.
Net cash of about INR193 crore is earmarked for the 300 MW under construction and pipeline wind projects.
demand_pricing: Data center order book rose from INR400-500 crore to INR900 crore as of July 31, 2026, and INR1,100 crore as of Aug 7, including a single order of over INR200 crore.

Price hikes taken in two phases: a small increase mid-Q1 and the balance at start of Q2. Quantum not disclosed; management cited a 10-15% range as not accurate. Old orders executed at pre-hike prices, new orders quoted at new prices.
Management expects one or two quarters for price pass-through, citing CPCB IV+ precedent of ~33% price increase over 9 months.
Manufacturing is the largest end market by share, followed by real estate; rentals and commercial are among the faster-growing segments.
Management said competition in data centers is rising, but it cites execution reputation; no market share data available.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow and order book comparison vs March 2025/2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book as of July 31, 2026 is up 15-19% YoY versus the same quarter last year, depending on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Genset margin outlook and whether the order book is fixed-price?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are impacted by the West Asia crisis for Q1 and part of Q2, improving from Q3. Older orders have fixed prices, with some price hikes obtained; new orders carry new prices.

qa_highlights.question: Data center BOP share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: BOP execution is about 30% of data center project value. Margins vary order to order by volume, delivery timeline, engine requirement and customisation; no fixed margin given.

qa_highlights.question: DG capacity utilisation and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-80% on one shift; current capacity is sufficient, with expansion planned if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Wind PPA timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction. The 50 MW GUVNL PPA is expected by Nov-Dec 2026 after LOA and about 90 days. The 100 MW SECI PPA is pending SECI's call.

qa_highlights.question: Wind EBITDA margins by project type?
qa_highlights.answer: New projects earn 82-83% EBITDA per management, old 330 MW projects 62-63%, EPC 10-11%. Analysts noted these figures as stated by management.

risks_watch: Genset margin (5.6% in Q1) recovery depends on whether price hikes stick over one or two quarters amid high commodity and energy prices.
Old data center orders were priced before the hikes, so margin may stay below the new-order level until they execute.
MSLG order inflow slowed because international inquiries were paused by the geopolitical situation; the pipeline is not yet quantified.
Wind PPAs for the 50 MW GUVNL and 100 MW SECI projects are still pending, and commissioning depends on them.
Competition in data centers is rising, and management said it lost two direct data center projects to Cummins in the past (per analyst).
